Reuse narrative knowledge with R agents

Source: vignettes/ecosystem.Rmd
ecosystem.Rmd

A research conclusion, reading interpretation, preference, or unresolved question can be ordinary record content. data-dict describes its fields and relationships; Graft adds reviewed acceptance, history and pinned reads. The application decides what the content means and who may use it.

Try the narrative workflow offline

This teaching example uses synthetic records and the shipped resolved dictionary. It requires neither a model nor the data-dict CLI. Source the example into a local environment, then run it:

example <- new.env()
sys.source(system.file("examples/narrative-knowledge.R", package = "graft"), example)
result <- example$narrative_example()
result$rejected[, c("field", "message")]
#>       field                                           message
#> 1 source_id Reference target `source:missing` does not exist.
result$pinned$body
#> [1] "## Reading interpretation\n\nThe café report suggests a local effect, not a universal result."
result$current$body
#> [1] "The synthetic report supports only a preliminary interpretation."
result$history[, c("revision_number", "producer")]
#>   revision_number      producer
#> 1               2 teaching-host
#> 2               1 teaching-host

The example rejects a missing evidence target, accepts corrected records, pins a reading, and accepts a later correction. The earlier reading retains its original meaning. A preference has no fabricated evidence link; its purpose is reading selection. Multiple evidence anchors are normalized support records.

The fixture is not Tempest’s promotion schema or a Rill integration. Applications keep their richer contracts. A stored archived value remains readable through ordinary Graft APIs; it does not enforce automatic-consultation eligibility. Likewise, restricted fields are omitted from public reads, but an owner_binding column does not establish Reader authorization.

Compose public tools with a host

Create one pinned tool set after the host has authorized the store and selection:

store <- graft_open(graft_schema(system.file(
  "extdata/narrative-knowledge.data-dict.json", package = "graft"
)), okf = "disabled")
graft_ingest(store, example$narrative_records(),
  graft_provenance("example-host", idempotency_key = "example-1"))
#> $batch_id
#> [1] "graft:5SDV225TB4XWB6TMHHPN7PW2RC"
#> 
#> $inserted
#> knowledge    source   support 
#>         4         1         2 
#> 
#> $updated
#> knowledge    source   support 
#>         0         0         0 
#> 
#> $matched
#> knowledge    source   support 
#>         0         0         0 
#> 
#> $observed
#> knowledge    source   support 
#>         4         1         2 
#> 
#> $warnings
#> character(0)
#> 
#> $duration
#> [1] 0.624
#> 
#> $replay
#> [1] FALSE
view <- graft_at(store, graft_snapshot(store))
tools <- graft_tools(view, result_format = "json")
value <- tools$graft_get("knowledge:preference")
jsonlite::fromJSON(value, simplifyVector = FALSE)$result$record
#> $id
#> [1] "knowledge:preference"
#> 
#> $kind
#> [1] "preference"
#> 
#> $purpose
#> [1] "reading selection"
#> 
#> $body
#> [1] "Prefer short reading sessions in the morning; this is a preference, not source evidence."
#> 
#> $lifecycle
#> [1] "active"
#> 
#> $tags
#> [1] "reading"

A host supplies its own configured Chat, credentials, permissions, context policy and execution lifetime. These are alternative recipes for that same tools list; the model calls are optional and are not run when building this guide:

# ellmer
chat$set_tools(tools)
chat$chat("Read the accepted interpretation and quote its basis.")
graft_verify(chat)

# Deputy: retain canonical results in the transcript for this bounded recipe.
agent <- deputy::Agent$new(chat = chat, tools = tools,
  context_policy = deputy::ContextPolicy(
    max_tokens = NULL, max_tool_result_bytes = NULL
  ))
agent$run_sync("Read the accepted interpretation and quote its basis.")
graft_verify(chat)

# Current dsprrr uses the dedicated react() constructor.
module <- dsprrr::react(dsprrr::signature("question -> answer"),
  tools = tools, chat = chat)
answer <- dsprrr::run(module, question = "What does the interpretation say?")
graft_verify(chat)

Use a fresh Chat for each host. The tests execute these public paths with actual objects and a loopback-only HTTP/SSE server: pinned reads after later acceptance, Unicode/Markdown, row truncation, missing IDs, and mixed non-Graft evidence. Verification consumes the actual ellmer Chat. Deputy run events or dsprrr’s summary metadata are not a substitute transcript. dsprrr’s final structured answer is not a completed text-bearing answer classified by graft_verify(); inspect the recorded text answers it actually contains.

A tool name collision must be checked before combining host and Graft tools:

combined <- c(tools, host_tools)
tool_names <- vapply(combined, function(tool) tool@name, character(1))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(tool_names))
chat$set_tools(combined)

Check the ToolDef name, not just its outer list name. ellmer replaces an existing name with a message, dsprrr retains the supplied tools and registers them with ellmer, and Deputy rejects duplicate registration. This host-side check avoids relying on different collision behavior. It does not require a Graft adapter.

Preserve results without overstating verification

Use graft_tools(view, result_format = "json") for ellmer, Deputy, and dsprrr. Each tool returns the complete envelope as an explicit json-class string, a supported ellmer return type. Graft uses the same JSON encoding as its accepted records. Its verifier decodes the envelope and applies the same receipt and citation checks; malformed JSON and duplicate object keys fail closed. A cited narrative requires an explicit matching quotation. Mixed non-Graft evidence or a failed tool cannot become verified because another tool returned a Graft receipt.

The default graft_tools(view) still returns ordinary R list envelopes. Existing $result and $receipt access, data frames, and attributes are preserved. Choose result_format = "list" explicitly when that R representation is required. Registering list-mode tools with ellmer 0.5 still uses its deprecated implicit conversion; switch registration to JSON mode instead of suppressing warnings. The return format is fixed at construction and never depends on call context.

r_tools <- graft_tools(view, result_format = "list")
envelope <- r_tools$graft_get("knowledge:interpretation")
envelope$receipt$boundary$kind
#> [1] "snapshot"

json_tools <- graft_tools(view, result_format = "json")
value <- json_tools$graft_get("knowledge:interpretation")
decoded <- jsonlite::fromJSON(value, simplifyVector = FALSE)
all.equal(decoded$receipt, envelope$receipt)
#> [1] TRUE

Decoded JSON has JSON’s types and arrays; it does not restore R data-frame classes or attributes. Use list mode when those R details matter. Both modes preserve the public content and accepted-boundary receipt. Direct public reads, including graft_dictionary(), keep their existing return types.

Bounds have distinct meanings. Search/history and related-record limits bound rows. Dictionary discovery additionally bounds text. graft_get() retains the full public narrative field and does not offer text pagination or a character ceiling. Size the authorized records and context budget accordingly.

Deputy’s default context policy may offload a large result to a durable reference. The host can retrieve the exact R value with agent$resolve_tool_result(reference); the model has a bounded deputy_read_tool_result path. Tests recover a long Unicode/Markdown JSON result byte for byte and a list-mode R envelope exactly. The offloaded reference/preview is not the canonical Graft envelope, so graft_verify() reports that evidence path as untrusted. Disabling offloading in the recipe above is an explicit choice for a bounded example, not a general recommendation for large documents.

For complete selection, dependency review and current consultation policy, see Retain an exact reuse basis.

Reconnect in the process that reads

A live DuckDB connection belongs to its process. Keep serializable, host-trusted references and reconstruct a view in a worker. The regression test closes the store before a fresh R process opens it read-only and verifies a complete selected record/evidence set. Do not deserialize arbitrary untrusted RDS content.

# Host-owned checkpoint: retain the full selection on unchanged days.
basis <- list(snapshot = graft_snapshot(store), ids = selected_ids,
  revisions = selected_revision_ids)
saveRDS(basis, checkpoint_path)
graft_close(store)

# In the worker: schema_path and store_path come from the authorized host.
basis <- readRDS(checkpoint_path)
store <- graft_open(graft_schema(schema_path), store_path,
  read_only = TRUE, okf = "disabled")
view <- graft_at(store, basis$snapshot)
records <- lapply(basis$ids, function(id) graft_get(view, id))
graft_close(store)

A snapshot identifies a boundary, not which records a task selected or permission to access them. A full selected basis includes evidence and exact revisions; new change receipts do not replace it. Eligibility, Reader scope, permanent Forget and backup/restore remain explicit design/integration work.

Ecosystem ownership and delivery status

Package Owns Evidence in this slice
data-dict Types, dictionary meaning, expressions Real producer export and profile probes
Graft Acceptance, identity, revisions, bounded reads, Definitions, Receipts Offline narrative/correction/worker tests
ellmer Chat, ToolDef, model transport Real Chat/tool loop with synthetic HTTP responses
Deputy Permissions, execution, offloading, host lifecycle Real Agent loop and exact offloaded-result recovery
dsprrr Modules, signatures, execution Real react() loop and proposal signature
Commons Detached public source, file measures, fallback labels Existing detached-source compatibility suite; unpinned
Tempest Scientific evidence, research products, promotion Existing public contracts inventoried; full reuse proof in #50
Rill Readers, Documents, accepted reading outcomes, Archive/Forget ADR-defined ownership; runtime proof and privacy gates in #47/#48/#51
scans/vitals Evaluation Task-quality evaluation remains in #41

Acceptance is not factual truth, access permission or authority to execute saved code. Graft Definitions retain their reviewed expression contract; Commons file measures remain separate trusted functions. No companion schema is needed for this teaching workflow. The backlog tracks the remaining application and lifecycle proofs separately.

Reproduce compatibility evidence

From a checkout with the optional hosts installed:

Rscript tools/check-host-composition.R
GRAFT_TEST_DATA_DICT_CLI=/path/to/data-dict \
  Rscript -e 'devtools::test(filter = "^data-dict-narrative$", stop_on_failure = TRUE)'

The host runner prints installed package versions and available source revisions. Tests do not install dependencies or contact model providers. See the compatibility guide for installation and the exact tested producer versions, and data-dict contracts for the narrower Graft adapter profile.
